reason: The text explicitly presents Yahweh articulating his intentions toward Abram: to make him a great nation (גוֹי גָּדוֹל), to bless him, to magnify his name, and to bless through him all families of the earth. Since Abram is the patriarch whose descendants become the Hebrew people, and Yahweh's stated goals include creating a great nation from him and extending blessing through his line, the text demonstrates that assisting Abraham and his progeny—who will constitute the Hebrew people—is indeed one of Yahweh's expressed goals. The narrative establishes this covenantal promise as foundational to the relationship between Yahweh and the Hebrew people.
